title: Objective
description: Something a person in the world wants done, given to the party in a scene (design/objectives.md). The RULE: every objective has a giver, is shown in the giver's own words, makes sense from the giver's side, and marks each part required or optional. Authored in canon/objectives/ and copied to data/objectives/ by `node tools/story/story.mjs build`. The Scene Runner gives, ticks, reveals, strikes and closes it through `objective` triggers in a scene's beats. Only the player-facing fields are ever written onto the Foundry page: `want`, `notes` and any part still hidden stay here.

id.description: Same as the file name. The c1e1- prefix is the Chapter and Episode it belongs to.

episodeRef.description: The episode it belongs to. An episode gives at most four group objectives.

kind.description: Who gave it. order: the chain of command (a direct order carries D053's weight). request: anyone else asked, and it can be turned down. own: a character decided it (players write these; the story rarely does).

direct.description: order only. Given in person by a superior, so refusing it is the serious offence the Deputy Director warns about (D053). A direct order must state its cost.

scope.description: group: the whole section. character: one character's, resolved at play to whoever it was given to.

npcRef.description: The giver's cast npcRef in the giving scene. Null for a giver who is only a signature on a paper.

name.description: What the table calls them when it is given. The tracker shows this.

via.description: How it came: "in person", "by letter, Form 1-A".

faction.description: The colour of their ring: vermilion, amber or cyan, the token-ring colours.

sceneRef.description: The canon scene that gives it. That scene must hold a `give` trigger for it.

handoutRef.description: When it came on paper: the handout in that scene. Its words are checked against the handout's body.

said.description: The giver's own words as they gave it, quoted on the tracker. Each part between " … " must appear word for word in the giving scene (or its handout).

title.description: Short and imperative, as the party would say it: "Clear the storm drain".

brief.description: One sentence: what the party understands is wanted, from the giver's side.

want.description: GM only. Never written onto the Foundry page.

motivation.description: The giver's underlying concern, from the nine (design/quests-objectives-and-threads.md §2).

stated.description: What they say it is for, if they say.

day.description: The campaign day (the orb's Day N).

quarter.description: The quarter it falls in. The chip turns solid when the world reaches it.

cost.description: What missing it costs, in the world's words. Required for a direct order (doctrine Law 19).

detail.description: What is needed, where and from whom: the explained view. Only what the table has been told.

by.description: Whose idea this part is, when it isn't the giver's: "Manako's idea", "Taka".

hidden.description: Not on the page until a `reveal` trigger adds it, so a player's browser never holds it early.

earned.description: Only revealed when a roll earns it. Shown with an EARNED tag.

strikeNote.description: For a part a `strike` trigger crosses out: why, as the table learns it.

moreHint.description: Show "There may be more to this" while any part is hidden. Off by default: the hint can give a twist away.

closes.description: What counts as done, plainly enough to recognise at the table.

suggestedRecord.description: A draft of the paragraph for the Record. The GM writes the real one when closing it.

facts.description: Canon facts its player-facing words tell. Each must be told by the giving scene.

notes.description: GM notes. Never written onto the page.
